items.followUp: Differentiate between an atom and a molecule.

rubric.why: A molecule is electrically neutral and consists of chemically bonded atoms.
rubric.description: Defines a molecule as a neutral group of chemically bonded atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for neutrality and 1 mark for the bonded-atom description; both are required for full credit here.

rubric.why: A molecular ion is a bonded group of atoms carrying an overall charge.
rubric.description: Distinguishes a molecular ion by its net charge and identifies it as a group of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is charged and 1 mark for identifying it as a group of atoms or giving a valid molecular-ion example.

modelAnswer: A molecule is an electrically neutral group of two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
A molecular ion is a group of two or more bonded atoms that carries an overall positive or negative charge.
For example, NH₄⁺ and SO₄²⁻ are molecular ions.

items.followUp: Define a coordinate covalent bond and explain its formation in the ammonium ion.

rubric.why: The defining feature is that the shared electron pair comes entirely from one atom.
rubric.description: Defines a coordinate covalent bond as a shared pair of electrons donated by one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a pair is shared and 1 mark for stating that one atom supplies both electrons.

rubric.why: The nitrogen atom in ammonia donates its lone pair to a hydrogen ion to form NH₄⁺.
rubric.description: Gives the ammonium-ion example with the correct donor and acceptor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying NH₃ (ammonia) and H⁺ as the species forming the coordinate bond.

rubric.why: The oxygen atom in water donates a lone pair to H⁺ to form H₃O⁺.
rubric.description: Gives the hydronium-ion example with the correct donor and acceptor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying H₂O (water) and H⁺ as the species forming the coordinate bond.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the shared pair of electrons is donated by one atom.
In the ammonium ion, NH₃ donates a lone pair from nitrogen to H⁺, forming NH₄⁺.
In the hydronium ion, H₂O donates a lone pair from oxygen to H⁺, forming H₃O⁺.
An arrow may be used to show the direction of donation, from the donor atom to the acceptor.

items.followUp: Define boiling point and state two factors that affect it.

rubric.why: Vapour pressure is the pressure of a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid in a closed system at a specified temperature.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure in terms of equilibrium between liquid and vapour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the pressure exerted by the vapour and 1 mark for stating that it is in equilibrium with the liquid.

rubric.why: Increasing temperature increases vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Identifies temperature as a factor and gives its effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that vapour pressure increases as temperature rises.

rubric.why: The nature of the liquid, particularly the strength of its intermolecular forces, affects vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Identifies the nature of the liquid or intermolecular forces as a factor and gives its effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that stronger intermolecular forces lower vapour pressure, or that more volatile liquids have higher vapour pressure.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid in a closed container at a particular temperature.
Temperature affects vapour pressure: as temperature increases, vapour pressure increases.
The nature of the liquid also affects vapour pressure: stronger intermolecular forces give a lower vapour pressure, while more volatile liquids have a higher vapour pressure.

items.followUp: Write four properties of a colloidal solution.

rubric.why: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
rubric.description: States that a suspension is heterogeneous.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

rubric.why: Suspended particles are large enough to be seen with the naked eye.
rubric.description: States that suspension particles can be seen with the naked eye.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

rubric.why: Suspension particles settle when the mixture is left undisturbed.
rubric.description: States that particles settle on standing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

rubric.why: Suspension particles can be separated from the liquid by filtration.
rubric.description: States that the components can be separated by filtration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
Its particles are large enough to be seen with the naked eye.
The particles settle down when the suspension is left undisturbed.
The particles can be separated from the liquid by filtration.

items.followUp: Write the symbols of lead and gold.

rubric.why: The chemical symbol for arsenic is As.
rubric.description: Gives the symbol for arsenic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for As.

rubric.why: The chemical symbol for silver is Ag.
rubric.description: Gives the symbol for silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Ag.

modelAnswer: Arsenic: As
Silver: Ag

items.followUp: Explain how cations and anions are formed.

rubric.why: A cation is positively charged because it loses one or more electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies a cation as a positive ion formed by loss of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both the positive charge and electron loss.

rubric.why: An anion is negatively charged because it gains one or more electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies an anion as a negative ion formed by gain of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both the negative charge and electron gain.

modelAnswer: A cation is a positively charged ion formed when an atom loses one or more electrons.
An anion is a negatively charged ion formed when an atom gains one or more electrons.

items.followUp: Describe the nuclear model of the atom proposed by Rutherford.

rubric.why: In Thomson’s model, the atom was represented as a positively charged sphere containing embedded electrons.
rubric.description: Describes the positive sphere and embedded electrons in the plum pudding model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons are embedded in a positive sphere.

rubric.why: The model is called the plum pudding model, and the atom as a whole is neutral because its positive and negative charges balance.
rubric.description: Identifies the model or explains the atom’s overall neutrality.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the plum pudding model or stating that the charges balance to make the atom neutral.

modelAnswer: The plum pudding theory was proposed by J. J. Thomson.
It described the atom as a sphere of positive charge with negatively charged electrons embedded in it, like plums in a pudding.
The positive and negative charges balance, so the atom is electrically neutral.

items.followUp: Define atomic number and mass number, and give an example of isotopes.

rubric.why: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers, due to different numbers of neutrons.
rubric.description: Defines isotopes by their same atomic number and different mass numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both features, or for stating the same proton number and different neutron numbers.

rubric.why: A valid pair of isotopes illustrates the definition.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of isotopes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid isotope example, such as carbon-12 and carbon-14 or hydrogen-1 and hydrogen-2.

modelAnswer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
For example, carbon-12 and carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon.
